paths.description: Homepage and featured listing: global navigation, search, card grid, preferences, responsive layout, performance, privacy and memory. Represents other paginated listing pages.
Taxonomy/index archetype with dense navigation and localized catalogue links.
Representative video detail and primary playback journey, including metadata and media accessibility.
Primary search results flow reached from the homepage GET form.
Authentication/form archetype, native invalid-state behavior and input assistance.
Network/HTTP recovery state using a guaranteed nonexistent route.

findings.summary: Theme is fixed rather than preference-driven
findings.evidence: Computed styles report color-scheme: normal and the dark/contrast capture remains the same fixed dark palette; no prefers-color-scheme adaptation was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark tokens with light-dark() or a prefers-color-scheme query.

findings.summary: Text and controls do not consistently meet contrast needs
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed the color-contrast audit, and no prefers-contrast or forced-colors adaptation was found in the inspected page styles.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct failing color pairs to WCAG thresholds and add forced-colors/prefers-contrast treatment for essential controls.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use View Transitions
findings.evidence: The DOM/style probe found no view-transition CSS or active transitions across the multi-page navigation surfaces.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same-origin navigation with cross-document View Transitions and reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Navigation chrome does not respond to scroll state
findings.evidence: The page installs a JavaScript scroll handler, but the inspected CSS and screenshots show static chrome rather than declarative scroll-state-aware feedback.
findings.suggestedFix: Use sticky chrome with scroll-state container queries or a lightweight progress affordance, with a fallback where needed.

findings.summary: Navigation changes provide little attention guidance
findings.evidence: Pagination and route links perform abrupt document changes without transition direction, highlight, or post-navigation focus cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Add clear current-page state and progressive directional transition/focus cues.

findings.summary: Advertising competes with the primary content above the fold
findings.evidence: Mobile and desktop screenshots show a large ad between search/navigation and the Featured Videos heading, consuming prime first-viewport space.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer or move advertising below the primary heading/content and preserve a content-first first viewport.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior relies on page-level rules rather than container-aware components
findings.evidence: The inspected stylesheet/probe found no @container/container-type use even though repeated cards and navigation components appear at multiple widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container queries for reused card and navigation components while retaining intrinsic fallbacks.

findings.summary: Lab LCP misses the good threshold on mobile
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 3.0 s and FCP at 2.6 s, although the local desktop trace was faster.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP resource, reduce render-blocking work, and validate mobile LCP below 2.5 s.

findings.summary: Caching and critical resource delivery leave avoidable delay
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 151 KiB cache savings, render-blocking requests and a font-display issue; HAR confirms parser-inserted CSS/scripts and missing image cache headers.
findings.suggestedFix: Set durable cache headers for versioned assets, use font-display, and defer or otherwise remove non-critical parser-blocking scripts.

findings.summary: The homepage ships substantial unused and legacy JavaScript
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 274 KiB unused JavaScript and 43 KiB legacy JavaScript; HAR shows scripts dominate transfer bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Split by feature, remove legacy transforms for Baseline-supported browsers, and defer third-party code until needed.

findings.summary: Several controls lack accessible labels or names
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails the select-name audit; the DOM probe found the country select and search input with zero associated labels plus unnamed buttons.
findings.suggestedFix: Associate visible labels or accessible names with every control and verify the accessibility tree.

findings.summary: Heading hierarchy is not sequential
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails heading-order; the probe shows H2 Menu before H1, then H3 and an empty H5. Keyboard focus itself remained visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Put the page H1 first in the content hierarchy, remove the empty heading, and keep levels sequential.

findings.summary: Video content has no caption track or equivalent
findings.evidence: The representative video detail contains two video elements and neither contains a track; the primary player exposes controls but no captions.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide synchronized WebVTT captions and an accessible transcript or equivalent for video content.

findings.summary: Image delivery uses legacy, non-responsive assets
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 60 legacy-format images, 61 without srcset, 58 below-fold images without lazy loading, 9 oversized images, and 2 missing dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP responsive variants, add srcset/sizes and dimensions, and lazy-load below-fold thumbnails.

findings.summary: Chrome reports browser inspector issues
findings.evidence: Lighthouse best-practices score is 0.77 and its inspector-issues audit fails.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve every DevTools Issues-panel item, then rerun Lighthouse and test BFCache/platform hygiene.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie attributes are incomplete
findings.evidence: Headers show no CSP, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy. All four observed cookies lack Secure and use SameSite=None; three persist for 400 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, clickjacking/referrer/permissions policies, and set Secure with appropriate SameSite and shorter retention on cookies.

findings.summary: A large third-party tracking footprint loads by default
findings.evidence: Trackers found 14 third-party origins including Google Tag Manager and DoubleClick. HAR attributes 26 of 44 requests and 606,723 of 791,432 transferred bytes to third parties.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise third parties, gate non-essential tracking behind informed consent, and batch or remove analytics.

findings.summary: Sign-in is password-only and omits modern authentication affordances
findings.evidence: The login form exposes username and password fields with no passkey/WebAuthn flow; autocomplete tokens are empty. No permission prompt was observed on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Add passkey authentication/registration as a progressive option and annotate fallback fields with correct autocomplete tokens.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent
findings.evidence: The main response lacks CSP/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy despite loading advertising and analytics from many origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Add least-privilege browser policies, starting with CSP and frame-ancestors, then tighten referrer and permission exposure.

findings.summary: The app-like media service is not installable or offline-capable
findings.evidence: A manifest exists but is generic (name App, icons only), and the service-worker registration probe returned no registrations.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a complete manifest and a conservative service worker with offline navigation/error fallback if installability is intended.

findings.summary: Location-targeted advertising is visually close to site content
findings.evidence: Screenshots show personalized dating/chat advertising directly above core content with only a small Ad badge, increasing the chance it is mistaken for site content.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase ad disclosure prominence and visual separation; never style sponsored actions like primary site actions.

findings.summary: Sign-in fields do not declare autofill semantics
findings.evidence: The login probe shows empty autocomplete attributes on both login and password fields.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete=username and autocomplete=current-password, retaining labels and password-manager compatibility.

findings.summary: Account access depends on a password-only login
findings.evidence: The inspected account entry offers only username/password, with no passkey option or visible modern reauthentication path.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey sign-in while keeping a clear, recoverable fallback and account-management path.

findings.summary: Thumbnail assets are not efficiently sized or encoded
findings.evidence: The image audit reports 60 legacy images, 61 without responsive sources and 9 oversized relative to display size.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve responsive AVIF/WebP thumbnails at the rendered size and lazy-load offscreen media.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts dominate homepage transfer
findings.evidence: HAR shows 606,723 bytes from third parties out of 791,432 total, led by tag manager, age verification and ad scripts; 14 third-party origins load on entry.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, defer non-essential scripts until interaction/consent, and remove duplicate analytics loads.

Improve account autofill and add passkeys
